content: On March 23, 2014, the Ministry of Health in Guinea informed the World Health Organization (WHO) about a rapidly escalating outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) in the forested southeastern regions of Guinea, specifically in the districts of Guéckédou, Macenta, Nzérékoré, and Kissidougou. By March 22, 2014, a total of 49 cases had been reported, including 29 deaths, resulting in a case fatality ratio of 59%. Among the victims were four healthcare workers. Concurrently, suspected cases in border areas of Liberia and Sierra Leone were under investigation. Six blood samples were tested at the Institut Pasteur in Lyon, France, and confirmed positive for the Ebola virus via polymerase chain reaction (PCR), marking the first confirmed outbreak of EVD in Guinea. Preliminary genetic sequencing of the L gene revealed a strong similarity to the Zaire ebolavirus strain. In response, the Ministry of Health, in collaboration with WHO and other partners, initiated measures to control the outbreak and prevent further spread. Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) began operations in the affected areas, assisting in the establishment of isolation facilities and supporting the transport of biological samples from suspected cases and contacts to international reference laboratories for urgent testing. The Emerging and Dangerous Pathogens Laboratory Network (EDPLN) collaborated with the Guinean Viral Hemorrhagic Fever (VHF) Laboratory in Donka, the Institut Pasteur in Lyon and Dakar, and the Kenema Lassa Fever Laboratory in Sierra Leone to ensure the availability of appropriate filovirus diagnostic capacity in Guinea and Sierra Leone. On March 30, 2014, the Ministry of Health in Liberia provided updated information on suspected and confirmed EVD cases in the country. By March 29, seven clinical samples from adult patients in Foya district, Lofa County, were tested using PCR with Zaire ebolavirus primers at the mobile laboratory of the Institut Pasteur in Dakar, located in Conakry. Two of these samples tested positive for the Ebola virus. Among the suspected cases, there were two deaths: a 35-year-old woman who died on March 21 and tested positive for the virus, and a male patient who died on March 27 but tested negative. At that time, Foya was the only district in Liberia reporting confirmed or suspected cases of Ebola Hemorrhagic Fever. As of March 26, Liberia had 27 contacts under medical follow-up. A high-level National Task Force was established in Liberia to lead the response, with support from partners including WHO, the International Red Cross (IRC), Samaritan’s Purse (SP) Liberia, Pentecostal Mission Unlimited (PMU) Liberia, CHF-WASH Liberia, PLAN-Liberia, UNFPA, and UNICEF. On April 3, 2014, the outbreak was confirmed to be caused by a strain of the Ebola virus with 98% genetic similarity to the Zaire ebolavirus. This marked the first time the disease had been detected in West Africa. As of June 17, 2014, Guinea reported seven new cases and five new deaths, with four cases and five deaths in Guéckédou and three cases with no deaths in Boffa. This brought the cumulative total in Guinea to 398 cases (254 confirmed, 88 probable, and 56 suspected) and 264 deaths. The geographic distribution of cases and deaths in Guinea was as follows: Conakry (70 cases, 33 deaths), Guéckédou (224 cases, 173 deaths), Macenta (41 cases, 28 deaths), Dabola (4 cases, 4 deaths), Kissidougou (8 cases, 5 deaths), Dinguiraye (1 case, 1 death), Telimele (30 cases, 9 deaths), Boffa (19 cases, 10 deaths), and Kouroussa (1 case, 1 death). Currently, 24 patients were being treated in EVD treatment centers: six in Conakry, nine in Guéckédou, three in Telimele, and six in Boffa. Nationwide, 1,258 contacts were under follow-up, distributed as follows: Conakry (252), Guéckédou (529), Macenta (52), Telimele (118), Dubreka (118), and Boffa (189). Approximately 69% of contacts (2,848 out of 4,106 registered since the outbreak began) had completed the mandatory 21-day observation period. In Liberia, nine new cases and five new deaths were reported, with six cases and no deaths in Lofa and three cases and five deaths in Montserrado. This brought the cumulative total in Liberia to 33 cases (18 confirmed, 8 probable, and 7 suspected) and 24 deaths. The geographic distribution of cases and deaths in Liberia was as follows: Lofa (21 cases, 14 deaths), Montserrado (8 cases, 8 deaths), Margibi (2 cases, 2 deaths), and Nimba (2 cases, 0 deaths). Five patients were currently being treated in EVD treatment centers in Lofa. Nationwide, 108 contacts were under follow-up, distributed as follows: Lofa (95) and Montserrado (13). Approximately 42% of contacts (108 out of 260 registered since the outbreak began) had completed the mandatory 21-day observation period. In Sierra Leone, 31 new cases and four new deaths were reported, with 29 cases and four deaths in Kailahun, one case in Kono, and one case in Western. This brought the cumulative total in Sierra Leone to 97 cases (92 confirmed, 3 probable, and 2 suspected) and 49 deaths. The geographic distribution of cases and deaths in Sierra Leone was as follows: Kailahun (92 cases, 46 deaths), Kambia (1 case, 0 deaths), Port Loko (2 cases, 1 death), Kono (1 case, 0 deaths), and Western (1 case, 1 death). Thirty-three patients were currently being treated in the EVD treatment center in Kenema. Nationwide, 37 contacts were under follow-up, all from Kailahun. Contact tracing efforts were ongoing in Kailahun, Kambia, and Port Loko.
